new_defect.where: swap_field_party_slots, at the second cursor selection — choosing the target slot after the SWITCH command
new_defect.why_it_is_newly_reachable: Placing a trainee into slot one only happens once training actually starts. The previous run stopped before any of this, and every run before that stopped earlier still, so this path had never executed against the game.
new_defect.status: not yet diagnosed. select_cursor now reports the cursor readings it saw and which of the three menu stages failed, so the next run distinguishes a cursor that never moved — meaning this menu does not report itself at CURRENT_MENU_ITEM — from one that moved and did not arrive.

what_the_harness_did_not_catch.finding: The fake-emulator harness exercises this exact swap and passes. It models the party menu the way the code assumes the menu behaves, so it confirms the code runs and cannot confirm the model is right.
what_the_harness_did_not_catch.consequence: A fake that answers back catches missing symbols, wrong arity, unreachable branches and never-executed code. It cannot catch a wrong belief about the game, because the fake is built out of that same belief.
what_the_harness_did_not_catch.not_a_reason_to_drop_it: The harness has already turned four reintroduced defects red in milliseconds. This is a statement of its boundary, not an argument against it: memory layout and menu behaviour have to be measured against the game, and that is what the run is for.
